Introduction

FlowScope receives network flows, such as NetFlow/IPFIX and sFlow. It enriches them with interface names (using SNMP), and geographic information (using IPinfo or MaxMind). Then, it exports them to ClickHouse via Kafka. It also provides a web interface to explore the data.

A public instance filled with generated traffic runs on demo.akvorado.net. It is the best place to see what FlowScope looks like before installing anything.

Tutorials

The tutorials get your started. Start here if you have never used FlowScope and want to get results quickly.

  • Explore the demo site: learn to read the graphs, without installing anything.
  • Collect your first flows: install FlowScope and connect your first router to it.

How-to guides

The guides are recipes for a specific goal. They assume you already have FlowScope running.

  • Install FlowScope: the deployment options, the requirements, and the upgrade procedure.
  • Configure your exporters: the configuration snippets for Cisco, Juniper, Arista, Nokia, and a few others.
  • Troubleshoot FlowScope: find which component is at fault when the flows do not arrive.
  • Operate FlowScope: keep Kafka, ClickHouse and the Docker Compose setup in good shape.
  • Scale FlowScope: what to tune when packets are dropped or flows are late.

Reference

Reference guides are technical descriptions of the machinery and how to operate it.

  • Configuration: every configuration settings.
  • Command line and endpoints: the subcommands and the HTTP endpoints of each service.
  • Web console: the manual of the web interface and the filter language.
  • Metrics: every metric exported for monitoring.

Explanation

The following guides are for when you want to understand what happens behind the scenes.

  • How FlowScope works: the four services, the path of a flow, and how the data is stored.
  • Internal design: how the code is organized and why.

The changelog lists the changes of each version. Read it before every upgrade.

Getting help

Important

Please, do not open an issue or start a discussion unless you have read the various chapters of the documentation, notably the troubleshooting guide.

Questions go to the discussions on GitHub. Explain what you tried and what you observed, and include the output of the commands from the troubleshooting guide.

Colophon

FlowScope is based on Akvorado, developed by Free Mobile and licensed under the AGPLv3 license. FlowScope is licensed under the same terms.
